RESI for mgcv gam/bam: null check and point-estimate calibration

2026-11-18

  • Design
  • Null check
  • Calibration of the point estimates
  • Is Ref.df the right bias correction?
  • Standard errors
  • Interpretation

Design

Simulation from tests/run_gam_calibration.R (design and decisions: notes/resi_gam.qmd). The data are Gaussian with \(\sigma = 1\) and

\[y = \sin(2\pi x_1) + 0.5\,x_2 + 0\cdot x_3 + 0.2\,w + 0\cdot w_0 + \varepsilon,\]

where \(x_1, x_2\) are uniform and correlated through a Gaussian copula (\(\rho = 0.5\)), giving some concurvity. \(x_3\) is uniform, and \(w, w_0 \sim N(0, 1)\), all independent of each other and of \((x_1, x_2)\). Each replicate draws one data set per \(n \in \{200, 1000, 5000, 20000\}\) (500 replicates) and fits y ~ s(x1, k) + s(x2, k) + s(x3, k) + w + w0 with \(k \in \{10, 20\}\), using:

  • mgcv (penalized; the estimator under evaluation): gam(method = "REML") or bam() (default fREML). The smooth-term RESI is f2S(F, Ref.df, residual df, n) from summary(), i.e. mgcv’s Wald statistic with the Bayesian Vp and the Ref.df correction. The coefficient RESI is t2S(t, residual df, n).
  • unpenalized (reference): the same with fx = TRUE, an ordinary regression spline with \(k - 1\) df per smooth.

The targets are T1, the basis-free \(S_j\) (\(S_j^2 = E[\{f_j - \Pi_{-j} f_j\}^2]/\sigma^2\), with the projection computed on a \(2 \times 10^5\) sample with rich bases), and T2, the fixed-\(k\) regression-spline limit.

Null check

\(x_3\) (smooth) and \(w_0\) (parametric) have no effect. Under the null, the p-values should be uniform and \(\hat S\) should be close to zero.

Is Ref.df the right bias correction?

The \(-\text{df}\) correction removes the contribution of the estimator’s variance to \(E[T]\): \(E[T] = n S^2 + \operatorname{tr}\{V_r^-\operatorname{Cov}(\hat p)\}\) when \(\hat p\) is unbiased. mgcv’s construction makes this trace equal to Ref.df when Vp is the covariance of \(\hat p\). On the scale used by f2S, the diagnostic below is the effective df, \(E[F\,r\,(\text{rdf}-2)/\text{rdf}] - n S^2_{T1}\), compared with the MC mean of Ref.df. Penalization also shrinks the signal part of \(T\), so a negative gap mixes a too-large df with smoothing bias. The gap divided by \(n\) is the bias of \(\hat S^2\) before truncation. The MC SE of the effective df grows like \(\sqrt{n} S\), so the check is informative only for null and weak terms (s(x3), s(x2)); for s(x1) at large \(n\) it is noise.

Mean edf, mean Ref.df, and effective df = E[F Ref.df (rdf-2)/rdf] - n S_T1^2; S2_bias = (effective df - Ref.df) / n

Standard errors

For the coefficient of \(w\), the table compares the mean model SE (from Vp) with the MC SD of the estimate. For the smooths, Vp is a Bayesian covariance that includes the expected squared smoothing bias. Its pointwise SEs should therefore match the root MC mean squared error of \(\hat f_j\) on a grid of \(x\) (“across-the-function” calibration; Marra & Wood 2012), rather than the MC SD.

Interpretation

  • Null check. For the null smooth s(x3) and the null coefficient w0, rejection rates at 0.05 are 0.03-0.06 for every engine, \(k\) and \(n\), within Monte Carlo error of 0.05. The mgcv p-values (which ignore smoothing-parameter uncertainty) are not anti-conservative in this design. The null mean of \(\hat S\) is small and shrinks like \(n^{-1/2}\), as expected for a truncated estimator.
  • Point estimates are consistent for T1. For gam and bam, the relative bias of the mgcv RESI against the basis-free target T1 is -4% (s(x1)) and -12% (s(x2), small \(S\), so truncation matters) at \(n = 200\). It is -0.7% and -1.9% at \(n = 1000\), and below 1% at \(n \ge 5000\), for both \(k = 10\) and \(k = 20\). T1 and T2 coincide here (the bases represent both functions well).
  • The penalized estimator is less biased than the unpenalized regression-spline reference at small \(n\). The same holds for the coefficient of w (-5.6% vs -11% to -20% at \(n = 200\), \(k = 20\)). This is the usual \(O(p/n)\) effect: the unpenalized model spends \(3(k-1)\) df, which inflates the coefficient’s sampling variance relative to its population value. The penalized fit spends only its edf. It vanishes by \(n = 1000\)-5000.
  • Ref.df as the bias correction. For the null smooth, the effective df (\(E[T]\) under \(H_0\)) is about 1.65-1.75 against a mean Ref.df of 1.42-1.46. Ref.df therefore under-corrects by about 0.25, a bias of \(0.25/n\) in \(\hat S^2\), which is negligible next to its SE. The unpenalized reference matches \(k - 1\), as it should. For non-null terms the check is within MC error.
  • Standard errors. The model SE of the w coefficient matches its MC SD (ratios 0.98-1.05). The pointwise Vp SEs of the smooths match the MC RMSE within 0.91-1.08. The lowest ratios (about 0.91 at large \(n\)) are for the linear s(x2), where \(\hat\lambda\) is poorly identified (near the penalty null space). This is consistent with mgcv’s warning that smoothing-parameter uncertainty is ignored, and would be the first place to revisit Vc if intervals undercover.
  • Not yet covered: non-Gaussian families, stronger concurvity, wigglier functions where the basis dimension \(k\) is binding (where T1 and T2 separate), a real-data plasmode, and the SE of the RESI itself (needed for CIs, deferred by design).
